title: Power Round — Fall 2024 — ARML Power sub-problem rubric

criteria.name: Problem 1
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 1 (2 pts). Statement: 1. Given the restriction that Alice must choose a monomial, akxk, Bob can determine Alice’s polynomial by asking just two questions. Bob asks Alice to compute A = p(1) and B = p(2). Given the values of A and B, determine Alice’s polynomial. That is, compute the exact values of k and ak in terms of A and B

criteria.name: Problem 2
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 2 (2 pts). Statement: 2. Show that even if it is known that Alice has chosen a monomial, it is impossible for Bob to determine it by asking just one question. That is, for any x that Bob might choose, and given that p(x) = A, ﬁnd two diﬀerent monomials that could be Alice’s polynomial.

criteria.name: Problem 3
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 3 (2 pts). Statement: 3. Alice is restricted to choosing a polynomial of degree at most 1. Given the values A = p(0) and B = p(1), determine Alice’s polynomial (in terms of A and B).

criteria.name: Problem 4
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 4 (2 pts). Statement: 4. Alice is restricted to choosing a polynomial of degree at most 2. Given the values A = p(0), B = p(1), and C = p(−1), determine Alice’s polynomial (in terms of A, B, and C).

criteria.name: Problem 5
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 5 (1 pt). Statement: 5. Compute ℓj(ri) for any 1≤ i≤ k with i̸= j .

criteria.name: Problem 6
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 6 (1 pt). Statement: 6. Compute ℓj(rj).

criteria.name: Problem 7
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 7 (2 pts). Statement: 7. Given the restriction that Alice must choose a polynomial of degree at most k, prove that Bob can determine her polynomial by asking k + 1 questions.

criteria.name: Problem 8
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 8 (2 pts). Statement: 8. Given the restriction that Alice must choose a polynomial of degree at most k, prove that Bob cannot determine her polynomial by asking fewer than k+1 questions.

criteria.name: Problem 9
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 9 (2 pts). Statement: 9. Given the restriction that all the coeﬃcients in Alice’s polynomial are nonnegative integers less than 10, Bob asks Alice to compute p(10) and is told that the value is 364,208,592. Determine Alice’s polynomial.

criteria.name: Problem 10
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 10 (2 pts). Statement: 10. Given the restriction that all the coeﬃcients in Alice’s polynomial are either 0 or 1, Bob asks Alice to compute p(2) and is told the value is 593. Determine Alice’s polynomial.

criteria.name: Problem 11
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 11 (2 pts). Statement: 11. Given the restriction that all the coeﬃcients in Alice’s polynomial are either 0 or 1, explain how Bob can always determine Alice’s polynomial by asking Alice to compute the single value p(2).

criteria.name: Problem 12
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 12 (3 pts). Statement: 12. Given the restriction that all the coeﬃcients in Alice’s polynomial are nonnegative integers less than b, explain how Bob can always determine Alice’s polynomial with just one question.

criteria.name: Problem 13
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 13 (3 pts). Statement: 13. Given the restriction that all the coeﬃcients in Alice’s polynomial are nonnegative integers, explain how Bob can determine Alice’s polynomial with just two questions.

criteria.name: Problem 14
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 14 (3 pts). Statement: 14. Given the restriction that all the coeﬃcients in Alice’s polynomial are either 0, 1, or−1, Bob asks Alice to compute p(3) and is told the value is 1573. Determine Alice’s polynomial.

criteria.name: Problem 15
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 15 (3 pts). Statement: 15. Given the restriction that all the coeﬃcients in Alice’s polynomial are −1, 0, 1, 2, or 3, Bob asks Alice to compute p(5) and is told the value is 1238. Determine Alice’s polynomial.

criteria.name: Problem 16
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 16 (4 pts). Statement: 16. Given the restriction that all the coeﬃcients in Alice’s polynomial are integers in the interval ( m, n), explain how Bob can determine Alice’s polynomial with just one question. Note: m and n need not themselves be integers.

criteria.name: Problem 17
criteria.description: Correct, justified solution to Problem 17 (4 pts). Statement: 17. Problem 13 asked you to ﬁnd a way to determine Alice’s polynomial with just two questions, given that all of her coeﬃcients were nonnegative integers. Now assume that all of her coeﬃcients are integers, the leading coeﬃcient is positive, and the smallest coeﬃcient is known to be at least −n for some positive integer n. Explain how to determine Alice’s polynomial with just two questions.
